statement: Right now, the ages of a family of four (two parents and two children) add up to 100 years. In how many years will their ages add up to 120 years?

choices.misconception: I only let the two children grow older, but the parents get older too.
I thought the total goes up by 1 each year, but each of the four people adds 1, so it goes up by 4.
I divided 100 by 4 and gave the average age now instead of a number of years.
I divided 120 by 4 and gave the average age later instead of a number of years.

hints: How much does the total grow in one year?
Every year, each of the four people gets one year older. Work out how much the total of their ages goes up each year, then how many such years cover the difference.
The total must grow by 20 years, and it grows by 4 every year.

solutions.reliable: Each year all four people get one year older, so the total of their ages rises by 4 each year. It must rise from 100 to 120, which is 20, so it takes $20 \div 4 = 5$ years. The transferable idea: in age problems everyone ages at once, so a total of n ages grows by n each year.

whyOnTest: Age questions test that every person ages at the same time, so a total of several ages grows faster than one year per year.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
